headline: Koshi peaks above 316,000 cusecs then eases, 11 highways shut, 172 families out
dek: The Kathmandu Post counts 389 houses under water in Nawalparasi West and Saptari, and the Department of Roads has stopped night travel on the blocked highways.
body_markdown:
The Koshi barrage ran at 316,795 cusecs on Saturday morning with 43 of its 56 gates open, Himal Press reported. Later in the day Ekantipur reported the flow, which had crossed 300,000 cusecs, was falling.

The Kathmandu Post reports that Narayani and Saptakoshi flooding has put 389 houses under water in Nawalparasi West and Saptari, and that 172 families in Susta Rural Municipality in Nawalparasi West, Lumbini Province, were relocated on Friday and Saturday. The Post did not name the agency behind those counts. BBC Nepali reported the Susta flooding separately, with Deepak Raj Nepal, Chief District Officer of Nawalparasi Bardaghat Susta West, saying affected residents were being moved to safer ground.

## What is open, what is shut

The Department of Roads said in a written notice on Saturday that rain since Asoj 8, September 24, has blocked 11 highways and several road sections, as Radio Nepal and Rajdhani Daily reported. It has stopped night travel on the affected highways and barred daytime movement at points its divisions judge risky, as Prasashan reported. The notice names these among them: the Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir, Chaukibhir, Jawangkhola and Fishling, the Mid Hill Highway from Nisi Rural Municipality to Kanabagar, the Kaligandaki corridor at Jaimini-8 Belbagar, and the Baglung to Beni highway. Our sources do not carry the full list of 11.

District Police Office Kapilvastu said a landslide near Viral Danda blocked the Dang to Kapilvastu section of the East-West Highway at about 8pm on Saturday and stopped vehicles completely, Nepal Press reported. No reopening time has been given.

In Nawalpur the Kaligandaki swept away the approach road to a motorable bridge, cutting the Gandaki provincial road between Dedhgaun and Ghiring Rural Municipality in Tanahun, DC Nepal reported, citing Deputy Superintendent Anil Pandit of District Police Office Nawalparasi Bardaghat Susta East. Gorkhapatra reported that travel from Dedhgaun towards Bhimad, Damauli and Rampur of Palpa has stopped, with the detour running through Gaindakot and Ramdi.

On the Kanti Lokpath crews cleared the slides and the project banned night driving, OnlineKhabar reported, with the project office counting 27 places at high landslide risk, as Nagarik also reported. Chief District Officer Narahari Ghimire told OnlineKhabar that vehicles from Kathmandu are being held at Tikabhairab and those from Makwanpur at Chaugada. DC Nepal reported the Karnali Highway in Surkhet open for essential vehicles only, with the risk staying while the rain does.

## The rivers

Outlets give different gate counts for the Koshi barrage. Himal Press reported 23 gates open at about 165,000 cusecs on Thursday. It reported 24 gates at about 190,000 cusecs on Friday, and a flow of 229,000 cusecs later that day. On Saturday morning it reported 43 of the barrage's 56 gates open at 316,795 cusecs. Ratopati's English service put the Saturday flow above 316,000 cusecs with 43 gates open. Nagarik reported the flow above the barrage's danger level with 37 gates open. None of the reports we read give that danger level as a number. The three reports do not publish the time of their readings, so we cannot say which count is the later one.

Outlets described the Tinau at Butwal differently. DC Nepal, citing the Flood Forecasting Division, reported the level crossed the danger mark at 8pm on Saturday. Radio Nepal reported the same 8pm reading as above the warning level, and Lokaantar reported it the same way citing the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. One report calls it danger, two call it warning, and we could not establish which threshold the gauge crossed. The reports we read did not give the gauge reading in metres. The Flood Forecasting Division asked people on the banks and in low lying areas to stay on high alert until Sunday evening.

On the Narayani, Nepal Press reported the water crossed the alert level and neared the danger mark, and that Superintendent Rameshwar Paudel, chief of District Police Office Chitwan, said more rain could push it past danger. We paraphrase Paudel and Ghimire rather than quoting them, because we could not confirm verbatim wording in the reports we read. The Rising Nepal reported all gates of the Gandak barrage open and riverbank residents moved to safer ground.

No death or injury toll has been attached to Saturday's blockages. As of Saturday evening, neither the Department of Roads notice nor the district police reports cited here record a casualty, and we found no National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority figure for the day.

## Pokhara and the trekking season

In Pokhara the Seti has backed up into a lake at Ramghat, with informal settlements known as sukumbasi bastis in Pokhara-9 and Pokhara-11 and the riverside cremation grounds under water, DC Nepal reported. The Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation says Dhap Dam in Gokarneshwar Municipality-1 is fully safe and the water level has receded despite a landslide near the reservoir area, as Setopati, the Kathmandu Post and Republica reported. That is the ministry's own assessment.

The Annapurna Conservation Area Project head office in Pokhara, which sits under the National Trust for Nature Conservation, stopped issuing tourist permits for the Mustang area on Thursday, September 24, until the weather improves, OnlineKhabar reported from Mustang. The report does not say whether the halt covers the rest of the conservation area.

The Department of Roads notice sets no reopening time for any of the 11 highways. The next fixed marker is the Flood Forecasting Division alert, which runs to Sunday evening.

ranking.reason: The day's strongest service story: named officials, named districts and blocked highways from the Department of Roads, Flood Forecasting Division gauges, CDO and DSP quotes, plus the Annapurna permit suspension. Write it as a timestamped status report with every number tied to its outlet and hour, and note the conflicting Koshi gate counts (31/37/43) rather than picking one.

Confirmed at rank 1. It carries the widest base of named officials and places for a single day: Department of Roads via Republica, the Flood Forecasting Division on the Tinau, DSP Anil Pandit in Nawalparasi, CDO Deepak Raj Nepal on Susta, plus the ACAP permit suspension. Write it as a timestamped status report, cite the conflicting Koshi gate counts (31, 37, 43) with their outlets rather than picking one, and attribute the Dhap Dam safety line to the ministry.

findings.passage: Radio Nepal's English service put a figure on it and said continuous rainfall has disrupted 11 highways nationwide. Neither published a verified point by point list, so the count of blocked highways is still unsettled.
findings.problem: Both halves are wrong. The figure of 11 is not Radio Nepal's own count: the Department of Roads issued a written notice on Saturday saying 11 highways and various road sections are blocked by rain since Asoj 8. And a point by point list was published. Outlets carrying the notice name the sections: Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir, Chaukibhir, Jawangkhola and Fishling, the Mid Hill Highway at Nisi Rural Municipality to Kanabagar, the Kaligandaki corridor at Jaimini-8 Belbagar, and the Baglung to Beni highway. The article manufactures uncertainty about a number the source agency itself published, and denies two named outlets work they did.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: the Department of Roads said in a Saturday notice that 11 highways and several road sections are blocked, and list the named sections it gave. Drop the claim that the count is unsettled unless you can show a second agency count that conflicts.

findings.passage: Nagarik reported the flow above danger level with 37 gates open. OnlineKhabar's English service reported 31 gates. Ratopati's English service reported 43 gates and flow above 316,000 cusecs. All three were published inside roughly a day. Any single gate count is a snapshot, not a status.
findings.problem: The premise of the article's lead hook is false. The gate counts are not competing claims, they are a documented sequence as the river rose: 23 gates at about 165,000 cusecs on Sept 24, 24 gates at about 190,000 cusecs, 229,000 cusecs on Sept 25, then 43 of 56 gates at 316,795 cusecs on Saturday morning per Himal Press. The article withholds the timestamps that would explain the spread, omits that the barrage has 56 gates, and rounds 316,795 down to 'above 316,000'. Presented this way it reads as media confusion when it is an operations log.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the discrepancy framing with a timed sequence: flow and gates at each reported hour, the total of 56 gates, and the exact figure 316,795 cusecs. If you keep a media angle, say plainly that the counts rose with the river rather than implying outlets disagree.

findings.passage: The Koshi barrage shows how fast these figures decay.
findings.problem: The article never gives the latest figure it says readers need. Ekantipur reported on the same day that the Koshi flow, which had crossed 300,000 cusecs, was falling. Publishing a piece whose hook is that numbers decay, while stopping at a morning reading and never telling readers the river is receding, is the exact failure it accuses others of.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the most recent Koshi reading with its time and direction of travel, attributed to Ekantipur or the barrage office, before publication.

findings.passage: OnlineKhabar's English service reported 31 gates.
findings.problem: The 31 gate count does not appear anywhere in the Koshi coverage I could reach, and the OnlineKhabar English URL cited is not in the candidate feed supplied to the newsroom. Counts of 23, 24 and 43 are documented. A number that carries a third of the headline hook must be verified against the original outlet with a publication time.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-open the OnlineKhabar English story, record its publication time, and quote the count with that time. If it cannot be confirmed, remove the 31 figure from the body, the dek and the social hook.

findings.passage: A landslide near Viral Danda blocked the East-West Highway in Kapilvastu at about 8pm on Saturday.
findings.problem: The article contains no human toll at all. No deaths, no injuries, no missing, no national displacement figure from NDRRMA or Nepal Police, in a monsoon that has already killed hundreds in Nepal this year. A flood and landslide roundup that counts gates and road sections but not people is not the story a reader in Nepal or the diaspora is looking for tonight.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sourced casualty and displacement line high in the piece, or state plainly which authority has reported no casualties so far and as of what hour.

findings.passage: For families here and abroad watching relatives travel, the practical question tonight is simple. Which route is open, and which river is still rising.
findings.problem: The article poses the reader's question and never answers it. There is no list of open routes, no travel restriction line beyond Kanti Lokpath, and no current river levels. The Department of Roads notice also restricted night travel nationwide and daytime travel at spots judged risky, which is the single most actionable instruction of the day and is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Answer the question with a short sourced list of blocked sections and open detours, and add the Department of Roads restriction on night travel and on daytime travel at risky points.

findings.passage: ## Kathmandu, the hills and the trekking season
findings.problem: Bigger risk stories sitting in the newsroom's own candidate feed were dropped. The Seti has formed a lake at Ramghat in Pokhara with squatter settlements of Pokhara-9 and Pokhara-11 and cremation sites under water. Ekantipur reported damage at eight points on the Kavre section of the BP Highway with diversions washed away at five. The Jomsom to Korala road is blocked at multiple points, which the story brief itself listed. A Solukhumbu road link is severed. Any of these beats a ministry press line that a dam is fine.
findings.suggested_fix: Swap the Dhap Dam paragraph down and add the Seti lake at Ramghat, the BP Highway damage points and the Jomsom to Korala blockage, each attributed to the outlet that reported it.

findings.passage: Landslide shuts East-West Highway in Kapilvastu as rivers push past warning marks
findings.problem: The headline buries the payload the article itself says is the story. The dek and the social hook both lead on the Koshi barrage, and the hardest verified numbers in the piece are 43 of 56 gates open at 316,795 cusecs, 389 houses under water and 172 families moved. Instead the headline leads on one landslide reported at 8pm by district police, and 'warning marks' is vaguer than the sources, which say danger level on the Koshi and the Tinau.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead the headline with the biggest verified number, for example the Koshi at 316,795 cusecs with 43 of 56 gates open, or the 389 houses inundated, and move the Kapilvastu landslide into the body.

findings.passage: A landslide near Viral Danda blocked the East-West Highway in Kapilvastu at about 8pm on Saturday. District Police Office Kapilvastu told Nepal Press that soil and stones fell across the Dang to Kapilvastu section and that vehicle movement stopped completely.
findings.problem: The headline asserts a continuing shutdown from a single police report timed at about 8pm on the same evening, and the article never says whether clearing has started or when the road might reopen. The Nepal Press item indicates area police were at the site. A blockage reported minutes before publication can be cleared within hours, and the headline cannot cash that claim beyond the hour it was reported. Nepal Press also reports it through the police office, not as a direct statement to the outlet, so 'told Nepal Press' overstates the sourcing.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'District Police Office Kapilvastu said' and time-stamp the status as of 8pm Saturday. Add what police or the road division say about clearing work and expected reopening, or note that no reopening time has been given.

findings.passage: Radio Nepal and Lokaantar, citing the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, described the same 8pm reading as crossing the warning level. Both versions carry the same instruction.
findings.problem: Two problems. First, the attribution to NDRRMA is not supported by the Radio Nepal Nepali and Lokaantar items, which report the alert on the Tinau without that agency being the stated source in the text available, while DC Nepal cites the Flood Forecasting Division. Second, 'warning level' and 'danger level' are two different official thresholds in Nepali reporting, satarkata and khatara, so the two outlets may be reporting two different thresholds correctly rather than disagreeing. The article presents a possible threshold naming issue as a factual conflict and never gives the actual water level in metres.
findings.suggested_fix: Check who issued each reading, explain the two thresholds in one plain line, and give the gauge reading in metres against each threshold. Only call it a disagreement if the same threshold is described two ways.

findings.passage: Police information officer and Deputy Superintendent Anil Pandit told DC Nepal that the Kaligandaki swept away the approach road on the Nawalpur side of the motorable bridge
findings.problem: DC Nepal reports this 'according to' the information officer of District Police Office Nawalparasi Bardaghat Susta East, not as something he told DC Nepal. The article also drops the full name of his office, which matters because two Nawalparasi districts are in play in this story and one of them, Nawalparasi West, is where the 389 houses and Susta relocations are.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'DC Nepal, citing Deputy Superintendent Anil Pandit, information officer at District Police Office Nawalparasi Bardaghat Susta East, reported that...' and keep the two Nawalparasi districts distinct throughout.

findings.passage: The Kathmandu Post reported that Narayani and Saptakoshi flooding has inundated 389 houses in Nawalparasi West and Saptari, and that 172 families in Susta Rural Municipality were relocated on Friday and Saturday.
findings.problem: House rule says attribution is part of the fact. The Kathmandu Post did not count 389 houses itself, it reported an authority's count, and the article does not say which one. The BBC Nepali piece with Chief District Officer Deepak Raj Nepal on moving affected residents is in the sources list but never used, so the biggest human number in the article rests on a single outlet with no named official behind it.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the authority the Kathmandu Post cited for 389 and 172, and add the BBC Nepali line with CDO Deepak Raj Nepal as independent confirmation of the Susta relocations.

findings.passage: Neither published a verified point by point list, so the count of blocked highways is still unsettled.
findings.problem: This is a reputational claim about two named news organisations, and it is wrong. The same framing runs through the Koshi paragraph and the social hook, which sets three named outlets against each other on numbers whose times the article never checked. Publishing an accusation of sloppiness against named companies that the evidence contradicts is the kind of thing that draws a correction demand and undermines the masthead promise to check before publishing.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the implication that the outlets failed. If a media accountability angle survives at all, base it on timestamps you have actually recorded and say explicitly that the figures rose with the river.

findings.passage: Photo: “Flood gates on Koshi Barrage - panoramio” by bjornman via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
findings.problem: An undated stock photo of the barrage in normal conditions, with a bus and workers on the roadway per the alt text, sits on a breaking flood story about 43 open gates. Nothing labels it a file photo, so a reader will take it as today. The credit is also incomplete for CC BY-SA 3.0: there is no link to the file page, no link to the licence text and no share-alike notice. Panoramio imports on Commons carry varying licences, so the licence itself needs to be confirmed on the file page before publication.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'File photo' to the caption with the year if known, confirm the licence on the Commons file page, and give the full credit with links to the file and to the CC BY-SA 3.0 deed.

findings.passage: The project counts 27 risky stretches on that road.
findings.problem: The sources say 27 places on the Kanti Lokpath carry a high risk of landslide, which is why night driving is banned. 'Risky stretches' changes the unit from points to stretches, and 'the project' is the article's own vague attribution rather than a named office.
findings.suggested_fix: Write that the Kanti Lokpath project office counts 27 places at high landslide risk, attributed to Nagarik and OnlineKhabar.

findings.passage: The Annapurna Conservation Area Project has stopped issuing tourist permits from Thursday until the weather improves, OnlineKhabar reported, at the start of the autumn trekking season.
findings.problem: No calendar date for 'Thursday' in a piece published Saturday, and the decision maker is thinned out. The source says the decision was taken by the ACAP head office in Pokhara under the National Trust for Nature Conservation, to reduce possible disaster damage. There is also no figure for how many trekkers or permits are affected, which is what makes this matter to the diaspora and to trekking operators.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the date for Thursday, name the National Trust for Nature Conservation ACAP head office in Pokhara as the decision maker, and add a permit or arrival number if one is reported.

findings.passage: The Department of Roads says several highways are halted, Radio Nepal counts 11, and three outlets give three different gate counts at the Koshi barrage.
findings.problem: The dek is a list of what news outlets said, not what happened. It credits the count of 11 to Radio Nepal when the count belongs to the Department of Roads, and it spends its 153 characters on media bookkeeping instead of the flood. Nobody shares a dek about who counted what.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the dek around the hardest new fact the headline does not carry, for example the Koshi at 316,795 cusecs with 43 of 56 gates open and 172 families moved out of Susta.

findings.passage: District Police Office Kapilvastu told Nepal Press that soil and stones fell across the Dang to Kapilvastu section and that vehicle movement stopped completely.
findings.problem: The article carries no direct quotation anywhere, though house style requires quoting people in their own words. Three officials appear, Pandit, Paudel and Ghimire, and all three are paraphrased. Readers get the newsroom's voice where the sources offer spoken lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Pull one short direct quote from the Nepali sources, translated faithfully and attributed to the officer and the outlet, ideally SP Rameshwar Paudel on the Narayani.

red_team.summary: The article's central hook collapses under checking: the Department of Roads published the count of 11 blocked highways with the sections named, and the Koshi gate counts of 23, 24 and 43 are a rising river logged over three days, not three outlets contradicting each other, so both claims of unsettled numbers are wrong and one of them accuses named newsrooms of work they actually did. It also stops at a morning Koshi reading while Ekantipur reported the flow falling later the same day, carries no casualty or displacement toll beyond one Kathmandu Post figure with no named authority behind it, and drops bigger items from its own feed including the Seti lake at Ramghat in Pokhara and the BP Highway damage in Kavre. The reporting discipline on attribution and on the Dhap Dam caveat is real, but as written the piece leads on a single 8pm landslide, buries every hard number, hangs an unlabelled stock photo on a breaking flood story, and should not run until the highway count, the gate sequence and the human toll are fixed.

responses.response: The red team is right on both halves. The 11 figure belongs to the Department of Roads notice, not to Radio Nepal, and our own later paragraph names Krishnabhir, Chaukibhir, Jawangkhola and Fishling, which contradicts our claim that nobody published a point by point list. We have no conflicting agency count, so calling the number unsettled is manufactured doubt. Fix the attribution, carry the named sections, drop the doubt.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the second paragraph with: "The Department of Roads said in a written notice on Saturday that rain since Asoj 8 has blocked 11 highways and several road sections. Radio Nepal and Rajdhani Daily carried the notice. It names the points: the Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir, Chaukibhir, Jawangkhola and Fishling, the Mid Hill Highway from Nisi Rural Municipality to Kanabagar, the Kaligandaki corridor at Jaimini-8 Belbagar, and the Baglung to Beni highway." Add Rajdhani Daily to the sources list and delete the later duplicate sentence about the Prithvi Highway points.

responses.response: Accepted. If the counts are an operations log of a rising river, our discrepancy framing is wrong, and the barrage total of 56 gates plus the exact 316,795 cusecs are facts we withheld. Reframe as a timed sequence and keep the honest point that any single gate count ages within hours.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the Koshi paragraph with: "The Koshi barrage counts rose with the river. Himal Press reported 23 gates open at about 165,000 cusecs on Thursday, then 24 gates at about 190,000 cusecs and a flow of 229,000 cusecs on Friday, then 43 of the barrage's 56 gates open at 316,795 cusecs on Saturday morning. The outlets were not contradicting each other. Each was reporting the hour it had, which is why any single gate count ages within hours." Add Himal Press to the sources list.

responses.response: Fair hit. A piece whose hook is that figures decay must carry the latest figure and its direction. Add the Ekantipur reading.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the Koshi sequence: "By Saturday, Ekantipur reported that the Koshi flow, which had crossed 300,000 cusecs, was falling." Add Ekantipur to the sources list.

responses.response: Accepted. A number carrying part of the dek and the social hook has to be pinned to the original story with a publication time. We cannot show that time, and once the paragraph is rewritten as a rising sequence the 31 figure has no role. Remove it rather than defend it.
responses.proposed_edit: Delete "OnlineKhabar's English service reported 31 gates." from the body, remove the OnlineKhabar English Koshi entry from the sources list, remove "three outlets give three different gate counts at the Koshi barrage" from the dek, and replace the social hook with: "43 of the Koshi barrage's 56 gates are open at 316,795 cusecs, 11 highways are blocked and 172 families are out of their homes in Susta. Here is what is confirmed tonight."

responses.response: Accepted as a gap. A flood roundup that counts gates and not people is the wrong shape. One caution on the fix: the UN item is a season to date figure from August and cannot be presented as tonight's toll. The minimum honest repair is a sourced same day toll if one exists, and if not, a plain line saying no authority has issued one as of Saturday evening.
responses.proposed_edit: Add high in the piece, after the first paragraph: "No death or injury toll has been attached to Saturday's blockages. As of Saturday evening, neither the Department of Roads notice nor the district police reports cited here record a casualty, and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority has not published a figure for the day. The damage count so far is property. The Kathmandu Post reports 389 houses under water." If an NDRRMA or Nepal Police same day toll is published before we go out, replace this with the figure and the hour.

responses.response: Accepted. We asked the reader's question and then walked away from it. The nationwide night travel restriction is the most actionable line of the day and we left it out.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the Kaligandaki paragraph: "Here is what the notice tells drivers. The Department of Roads has stopped night travel on the affected highways and barred daytime movement at points its divisions judge risky, as Prasashan reported. responses.response: The style guide requires that quotes be in the speaker's own words and attributed, and it bans invention. The Nepali and English items we used report these officials in indirect speech, so there is no direct quotation for us to lift. Manufacturing quotation marks around a paraphrase would break rule 1, which outranks a stylistic preference. defense.summary: Accepted 17 of 18 findings. The two structural hits land: the 11 highway count belongs to the Department of Roads notice, which also published the named sections, and the Koshi gate counts are a rising sequence, not outlets disagreeing. Both errors fed the dek, the social hook and the defensibility finding, so the fix is one connected rewrite of paragraph two, the Koshi paragraph, the dek and the hook, plus removal of the unverifiable 31 gate figure. Also accepted: a new headline led by 316,795 cusecs and 43 of 56 gates, the latest falling Koshi reading from Ekantipur, a casualty and displacement line high in the piece, the night travel restriction that answers the reader's question, the Seti lake at Ramghat and BP Highway damage in place of a trimmed Dhap Dam passage, tighter attribution on Kapilvastu, Nawalparasi and the 389 houses, the warning versus danger threshold explanation, the file photo label and full licence credit. Contested one: we will not put quotation marks around paraphrased officials when the sources carry no direct speech, and we will add a quote only if the original Nepali text has one.

rulings.note: The count of 11 belongs to the Department of Roads notice, not to Radio Nepal, and the article's own later paragraph names Prithvi Highway points, which contradicts the claim that no point by point list exists. Manufactured doubt about an agency's published figure. Defence accepts.

Framing three counts as a disagreement without recording publication times is not defensible. The rewrite to a timed rising sequence is correct, but the editor must verify each figure and date against Himal Press and the barrage office rather than lifting the red team's numbers on trust.
A piece whose hook is that figures age must carry the latest reading and its direction. The Ekantipur line that the flow was falling is required.
An unverifiable number that carries part of the dek and the social hook cannot run. Remove the 31 gate figure and its source entry unless the original story and its publication time are confirmed.

A flood roundup with no human toll is the wrong shape. The defence's caution is right: the UN August season figure must not be presented as tonight's toll, and any 'no toll published' line must be limited to the sources actually checked.
The article poses the reader's question and abandons it. The night travel restriction is the most actionable instruction of the day and must appear, attributed to the outlet carrying the notice.
Seti lake at Ramghat and the BP Highway damage points outrank a ministry press line. Trimming Dhap Dam to one sentence rather than cutting it is a reasonable compromise.

The headline buries the hardest verified numbers and 'warning marks' is vaguer than the sources. The new headline must carry the time of the Koshi reading so it does not assert a status the falling flow contradicts.
'Told Nepal Press' overstates sourcing for a police office report, and a blockage reported at 8pm needs a timestamp and a line on clearing or the absence of a reopening time.
Warning and danger are distinct official thresholds, so presenting the two reports as a factual conflict is wrong, and the NDRRMA attribution must be pinned to the outlet that actually made it.
DC Nepal attributes to the office, not an interview, and the two Nawalparasi districts must be kept distinct because Nawalparasi West carries the inundation and relocation figures.
House rule: attribution is part of the fact. Name the authority the Kathmandu Post cited, or say plainly that the Post named none, and use the BBC Nepali line already in the sources.

The article makes a reputational claim against named news organisations that the evidence contradicts. This is the highest correction risk in the piece and must be removed entirely, including from the social hook.
An undated calm weather image on a breaking flood story reads as today. Label it a file photo, confirm the licence on the Commons file page and give the full credit with links, or pull the image.
Points are not stretches and 'the project' is not a named office. One line fixes it.
A bare 'Thursday' in a Saturday piece needs a calendar date and the decision belongs to a named office. Permit numbers only if the source reports them.
The dek reports media bookkeeping and misattributes the Department of Roads count to Radio Nepal. Rewrite around the hardest fact the headline does not carry.
The defence is right. Rule 1 outranks the quoting preference. Putting quotation marks around paraphrase would be invention. Add a direct quote only if the original Nepali text carries one.

required_edits: Headline: replace with a line led by the hardest verified number and timed, under 90 characters, for example: 'Koshi hits 316,795 cusecs Saturday morning, 43 of 56 gates open, 389 houses flooded'. Verify the exact cusec figure, the 43 of 56 gate count and the time against Himal Press or the barrage office before it runs. Move the Kapilvastu landslide into the body.

Dek: replace with a single sentence under 160 characters carrying facts the headline does not, for example: 'The Department of Roads says 11 highways are blocked and has stopped night travel on them, while 172 families are out of their homes in Susta.' Remove all reference to outlets giving different gate counts.

Paragraph two: replace with the Department of Roads notice as the source of the count. Write that the Department said in a written notice on Saturday that rain since Asoj 8 has blocked 11 highways and several road sections, name the sections the notice gives (Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir, Chaukibhir, Jawangkhola and Fishling, Mid Hill Highway from Nisi Rural Municipality to Kanabagar, Kaligandaki corridor at Jaimini-8 Belbagar, Baglung to Beni), and attribute to the outlets that carried the notice. Add those outlets to the sources list.

Delete the sentence 'Neither published a verified point by point list, so the count of blocked highways is still unsettled.' Delete every other implication that named outlets contradicted each other or failed to do their work.

Delete the later duplicate sentence attributing the Prithvi Highway landslide points to the Department of Roads via the Kathmandu Post if the same points now appear in the rewritten paragraph two, or merge the two so the points appear once.

Koshi paragraph: replace the discrepancy framing with a timed sequence. State the flow and gate count at each reported hour, the barrage total of 56 gates, and the exact figure 316,795 cusecs, each attributed to the outlet and dated. Every figure in the sequence must be checked against the original outlet before publication; do not carry any figure whose date and outlet cannot be named.

Delete 'OnlineKhabar's English service reported 31 gates.' from the body and remove the OnlineKhabar English Koshi entry from the sources list, unless the story and its publication time are confirmed and the time is printed.

Add after the Koshi sequence a sentence giving the most recent reading and its direction, for example that Ekantipur reported on Saturday that the Koshi flow, which had crossed 300,000 cusecs, was falling. Add Ekantipur to the sources list.

Add a human toll line in the first three paragraphs. If NDRRMA, Nepal Police or a district authority has published a same day death, injury or displacement figure, give it with the hour and the authority. If none exists, write plainly which sources were checked and that none of them records a casualty as of Saturday evening. Do not use the UN August season to date figure as tonight's toll.

Add the actionable travel instruction after the Kaligandaki paragraph: the Department of Roads has stopped night travel on affected highways and barred daytime movement at points its divisions judge risky, attributed to the outlet that carried the notice. Add that outlet to the sources list. Follow it with the open detours already in the piece, including the Gaindakot and Ramdi route and the Karnali Highway in Surkhet open to essential vehicles.

Opening paragraph: rewrite as 'District Police Office Kapilvastu said a landslide near Viral Danda blocked the Dang to Kapilvastu section of the East-West Highway at about 8pm on Saturday and stopped vehicle movement completely, Nepal Press reported.' Remove 'told Nepal Press'. Add what the sources say about clearing work, or state that no reopening time has been given.

Tinau paragraph: rewrite so DC Nepal citing the Flood Forecasting Division reports the danger mark, Radio Nepal reports the same 8pm reading as above the warning level, and Lokaantar reports it citing the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Add one plain line explaining that Nepal runs two thresholds, warning and danger, so the reports may name different marks rather than clash. State that none of the sources published the gauge reading in metres.

Kaligandaki paragraph: rewrite as 'DC Nepal, citing Deputy Superintendent Anil Pandit, information officer at District Police Office Nawalparasi Bardaghat Susta East, reported that...' and keep Nawalparasi West and Nawalpur distinct everywhere in the piece.

389 houses paragraph: name the authority the Kathmandu Post cited for the 389 and 172 counts, or write that the Post did not name the counting agency. Add the BBC Nepali line with Chief District Officer Deepak Raj Nepal on moving affected residents in Susta.

Cut the Dhap Dam passage to one sentence carrying the ministry claim and the caveat that it is the ministry's own assessment, not an independent inspection. Add in its place the Seti forming a lake at Ramghat in Pokhara with settlements in Pokhara-9 and Pokhara-11 and the cremation site under water, attributed to DC Nepal, and the eight damage points on the Kavre section of the BP Highway with diversions washed away at five, attributed to Ekantipur.

Kanti Lokpath: replace 'The project counts 27 risky stretches on that road' with 'The Kanti Lokpath project office counts 27 places at high risk of landslide on that road, Nagarik and OnlineKhabar reported.'

ACAP paragraph: give the calendar date for Thursday, name the Annapurna Conservation Area Project head office in Pokhara under the National Trust for Nature Conservation as the decision maker, state the stated aim, and say that OnlineKhabar gives no figure for affected trekkers or permits if none is reported.

Image: add 'File photo' to the caption and alt text, confirm the licence on the Wikimedia Commons file page, and give the full credit with a link to the file page and to the CC BY-SA 3.0 deed plus a share alike notice. If the licence cannot be confirmed on the file page, pull the image.

Social hook: replace with one carrying no claim that outlets disagreed, for example '43 of the Koshi barrage's 56 gates open at 316,795 cusecs, 11 highways blocked, 172 families out of their homes in Susta. Here is what is confirmed tonight.' Only use figures that survive the verification above.

Keep the body between 350 and 700 words after the edits, keep the closing line on what happens next with a date, and check that no banned phrase, em dash, semicolon or parenthesis has entered the rewritten passages.
judge_1.reason: The article's two load bearing claims are wrong: the count of 11 blocked highways belongs to a Department of Roads notice that also named the sections, and the Koshi gate counts read as a rising river logged over days rather than three outlets contradicting each other. That second error also puts an unsupported accusation of sloppiness on named newsrooms, which is the clearest correction and reputational risk in the piece. The reporting discipline elsewhere is real and the defence accepts almost everything, so this is fixable in one pass, but it cannot publish with a false hook, no human toll and an unlabelled calm weather file photo on a breaking flood story.

findings.passage: Koshi hits 316,795 cusecs, 43 of 56 gates open, 389 houses flooded
findings.problem: The headline states a Saturday morning peak as if it were the state of play at publication time on Saturday evening, and the article's own body contradicts it twice: Nagarik reported 37 gates open and Ekantipur reported the flow, having crossed 300,000 cusecs, was falling. It also welds the Koshi number to the 389 houses figure, which The Kathmandu Post attributes to Narayani and Saptakoshi flooding in Nawalparasi West and Saptari, not to the Koshi barrage alone. The 389 count carries no attribution in the headline even though the Post did not name the counting agency.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite to a time stamped, attributed headline, for example: 'Koshi peaks above 316,000 cusecs then eases, 11 highways still shut'. Move the houses figure to the dek with attribution to The Kathmandu Post.

findings.passage: Nagarik reported the flow above danger level with 37 gates open, and Ratopati's English service reported 43 gates and flow above 316,000 cusecs. Each outlet was reporting the hour it had.
findings.problem: The article invents a reconciliation it cannot support. It gives no timestamp for the Nagarik or Ratopati reports, yet asserts the discrepancy is a matter of different hours. The Nagarik item in the source set was published at 14:14 UTC, which is about 8pm Nepal time, later than the 'Saturday morning' 43 gate reading, so the claim that 'the counts rose with the river' is not established and may be backwards.
findings.suggested_fix: State the publication time of each report, or say plainly that the outlets give different gate counts and that the newsroom could not establish which reading is later. Delete 'Each outlet was reporting the hour it had' unless times are published.

findings.passage: Himal Press reported 23 gates open at about 165,000 cusecs on Thursday, then 24 gates at about 190,000 cusecs and a flow of 229,000 cusecs on Friday, then 43 of the barrage's 56 gates open at 316,795 cusecs on Saturday morning.
findings.problem: The Friday clause gives two different flows for the same gate count and reads as a garbled transcription. A reader cannot tell whether 190,000 and 229,000 are two separate readings on Friday or an error. The headline number 316,795 rests entirely on this one outlet, and the Himal Press link does not appear anywhere in the day's candidate set supplied to the newsroom, so it is unverified against any second source at that precision. Ratopati only supports 'above 316,000'.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the Friday readings into separate attributed sentences with times, and either confirm 316,795 against a second outlet or use the corroborated 'above 316,000 cusecs' in the headline.

findings.passage: No death or injury toll has been attached to Saturday's blockages. As of Saturday evening, neither the Department of Roads notice nor the district police reports cited here record a casualty, and we found no National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority figure for the day. The damage count so far is property.
findings.problem: The last sentence is a claim the newsroom owns and it goes beyond the checking described. Absence of a casualty line in a roads notice is not evidence that nobody died in a nationwide monsoon event, and the article did not check district reports from Solukhumbu, Mustang or Rolpa, all of which appear in the day's candidate list. One death report would make this line a correction.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut 'The damage count so far is property' and keep only the sourced negative: which specific documents the newsroom checked, at what time, and that NDRRMA had published no toll by then.

findings.passage: None of them published the gauge reading in metres.
findings.problem: A strong negative claim about three outlets. The DC Nepal Tinau report in the candidate set is cut off in the feed exactly at the point where the water level figure would appear, so the newsroom cannot know the metre reading was absent from the full article. Nepali flood stories routinely carry the metre reading and the danger threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the full DC Nepal, Radio Nepal and Lokaantar texts and publish the metre reading and the Tinau danger threshold, or soften to 'the reports cited here did not carry a metre reading'.

findings.passage: Ekantipur reported damage at eight points on the Kavre section of the BP Highway, with diversions washed away at five.
findings.problem: This claim has no traceable URL. The sources list attaches it to the Ekantipur Koshi barrage story, which is about a different river in a different province. The only BP Highway item in the day's candidates is a Google News aggregator link, which the house rules say to avoid in favour of the original outlet.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the direct Ekantipur BP Highway URL to the sources list as its own entry, or drop the sentence.

findings.passage: The notice names the points: the Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir, Chaukibhir, Jawangkhola and Fishling, the Mid Hill Highway from Nisi Rural Municipality to Kanabagar, the Kaligandaki corridor at Jaimini-8 Belbagar, and the Baglung to Beni highway.
findings.problem: The article says the notice blocks 11 highways and then presents a list of four as if it were the naming, leaving a seven highway gap the reader is never told about. The Rajdhani Daily link that carries this list is not in the day's candidate set, and the Jomsom to Korala road, which the story brief itself flags as blocked, is missing from the article entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'the notice names these among them' and add the Jomsom to Korala blockage reported by The Himalayan Times, or publish the full 11 with the Department of Roads notice reference number.

findings.passage: rain since Asoj 8 has blocked 11 highways
findings.problem: An English language article for readers in Nepal and the diaspora gives a Bikram Sambat date with no Gregorian equivalent. Asoj 8 is September 24, two days before the run date. Many diaspora readers cannot convert it, and it is the only date anchoring the whole weather event.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'since Asoj 8, September 24'.

findings.passage: The Annapurna Conservation Area Project head office in Pokhara, which sits under the National Trust for Nature Conservation, stopped issuing tourist permits on Thursday, September 24, until the weather improves, OnlineKhabar reported.
findings.problem: The OnlineKhabar item carries a Mustang dateline and says permits were stopped for tourists going to 'that area'. The article generalises this to a blanket halt on Annapurna Conservation Area permits. That is a bigger claim than the source supports and it affects trekkers planning trips right now.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the geographic scope exactly as the source states it, and if the scope is unclear say so and note that the newsroom asked NTNC for clarification.

findings.passage: Nepal runs two thresholds on its gauges, warning and danger, so the two reports may be naming different marks rather than clashing.
findings.problem: A factual explainer line with no source attached, in an article that attributes everything else. It is also speculation offered to smooth a genuine disagreement between outlets, which the house rules say to report as a disagreement.
findings.suggested_fix: Attribute the two threshold system to the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology or the Flood Forecasting Division, and state the disagreement without guessing at the cause.

findings.passage: Photo: “Flood gates on Koshi Barrage - panoramio” by bjornman via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
findings.problem: An undated archive photograph sits on a breaking flood story with nothing in the credit or alt text telling readers it is a file image, which invites the reader to believe they are seeing Saturday's barrage. The credit also gives no link to the Commons file page or to the licence deed, which CC BY-SA attribution practice expects, and the author string 'bjornman' has not been verified against the file page in this round.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'File photo' to the caption and alt text, link the Commons file page and the CC BY-SA 3.0 deed, and confirm the uploader name and licence on the file page before publication.

findings.passage: with squatter settlements in Pokhara-9 and Pokhara-11 and the cremation site under water
findings.problem: 'Squatter settlements' is a loaded English rendering of sukumbasi for people whose homes are flooding, and the DC Nepal report describes several cremation sites at Ramghat, Shantighat and a Buddhist monastery, not one. Flattening the detail weakens the translation fidelity rule and labels a vulnerable community rather than describing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'informal settlements known as sukumbasi bastis' and name the cremation sites the source names.

findings.passage: District Police Office Kapilvastu said a landslide near Viral Danda blocked the Dang to Kapilvastu section of the East-West Highway at about 8pm on Saturday and stopped vehicle movement completely, Nepal Press reported.
findings.problem: The headline sells Koshi at 316,795 cusecs and 389 flooded houses, then the piece opens on a single landslide in Kapilvastu and does not reach the barrage until the sixth paragraph, under a subheading. The payload the headline promises is buried, and the second paragraph is a negative finding about the absence of a casualty count, which is the weakest possible place to spend a reader's attention.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead with the Koshi barrage and the displaced families, put the road closures and the night travel ban second, and move the no casualty count line lower as a short sourced note.

findings.passage: Koshi hits 316,795 cusecs, 43 of 56 gates open, 389 houses flooded
findings.problem: Cusecs mean nothing to most readers and the article never says what the danger threshold is in cusecs, so the headline number carries no meaning and no shareable stake. The human hooks that would travel, 172 families out of their homes, Annapurna permits stopped at the start of the trekking season, a river turning into a lake in the middle of Pokhara, are all buried or in the last paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the danger threshold alongside the flow so the number means something, and raise either the displaced families or the Annapurna permit halt into the headline or the first two paragraphs.

findings.passage: On the Kanti Lokpath, OnlineKhabar reported that crews cleared the slides at Birkhedhara, Pangdur and Takurche and released stranded vehicles, while the project banned night driving.
findings.problem: The body runs 911 words against a house limit of 700 and contains no direct quotes at all, in an article naming five officials who spoke. It reads as a stacked list of outlet summaries rather than reporting, and the practical question a Nepal reader has tonight, which routes are usable tomorrow morning and which are not, is never assembled in one place.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut to 650 words, add at least two direct quotes from the officials already named, and consolidate the route information into a clear open or shut rundown.

findings.passage: BBC Nepali reported the Susta inundation separately, with Chief District Officer Deepak Raj Nepal saying affected residents were being moved to safer ground.
findings.problem: The official's district is omitted. BBC Nepali identifies him as CDO of Nawalparasi Bardaghat Susta West, and the article never tells readers which district or province Susta sits in, even though Susta is in the dek. Diaspora readers cannot place the story.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the full title and locate Susta for the reader on first mention, in Nawalparasi West, Lumbini Province.

findings.passage: The next marker is the Flood Forecasting Division's high alert window, which runs to Sunday evening.
findings.problem: The closing forward look is thin. It repeats a line already given earlier in the piece and offers no forecast, no reopening estimate for any of the 11 highways, and no indication of whether rain continues. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology forecast was not sought.
findings.suggested_fix: Close with the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology outlook for Sunday and any Department of Roads estimate for reopening, with a date.

red_team.summary: The reporting is careful about attribution and honest about what it could not confirm, but the headline oversells a morning peak that the article itself reports as falling and staples an unrelated houses count to it, and several load bearing figures trace to outlets that are not in the day's source set and were not corroborated. Two claims are stronger than the evidence behind them, the assertion that the damage is property only and the assertion that no outlet published a metre reading, and the BP Highway line has no matching URL at all. Structurally it is 911 words against a 700 word limit with no direct quotes, opening on a minor landslide while the promised Koshi and displacement news sits six paragraphs down, so it needs a re-cut headline, a re-cut lede and three sourcing fixes before it can run.

responses.response: The headline is a snapshot sold as a state of play, and the body itself reports the flow falling by Saturday and a lower gate count from Nagarik. Welding 389 houses to the Koshi line is also wrong: the Post attributes that count to Narayani and Saptakoshi flooding in Nawalparasi West and Saptari, and did not name the counting agency. We fix the headline to carry the peak and the easing, and move the houses figure into the dek with the Post named.

defense.summary: We accept 16 of 17 findings. The headline is rewritten to a time stamped, corroborated figure that carries the human stake, and the 389 houses count moves to the dek with The Kathmandu Post named. We cut the unsupported reconciliation of the gate counts, the owned claim that the damage is only property, the untraceable BP Highway sentence and the unsourced threshold explainer. We split the garbled Friday Koshi readings, soften the metre reading negative, narrow the Annapurna permit halt to the Mustang scope the source states, add the Gregorian date for Asoj 8, label the archive image a file photo, replace squatter settlements with sukumbasi bastis, locate Susta and give the CDO his full title, reorder to lead on the barrage and the displaced families, and trim the body from about 900 words to about 650 with a single routes rundown. We contest f17 only: the close already names what happens next with a date, and we will not publish a forecast or a reopening estimate we did not source. We also decline two sub requests inside accepted findings, the Jomsom to Korala blockage and a danger threshold in cusecs, because neither is in our sources.

rulings.note: The headline sells a Saturday morning peak as the state of play while the body reports the flow falling and a lower gate count from Nagarik, and it staples the 389 houses figure, which the Post ties to Narayani and Saptakoshi flooding, to the Koshi line with no attribution. The Friday clause gives two flows for one gate count and reads as garbled. The precise 316,795 is corroborated only at 'above 316,000' by Ratopati, so it belongs in the body with Himal Press named, not in the headline. Himal Press is a named outlet, so the sequence is attributed, but the split and the headline change are required.
'The damage count so far is property' is a claim the newsroom owns about a nationwide event on the strength of two documents. Keep the sourced negative, cut the summary sentence.
A blanket negative about three full articles the newsroom only partly read. Soften to what was read, as the defence proposes.

Sustained on burying the human stake. Overruled on printing a danger threshold in cusecs, since no source in the set gives one. The Nagarik 'above danger level' line plus the note that no report gives the number is the honest substitute.

About 900 words against a 700 word house limit, with no direct quotes from five named officials and no single place a reader can see which routes are usable. Trim and consolidate, quoting only verbatim wording the outlets print.
Susta appears in the dek and is never located, and the CDO's district is part of his title. One line fix.
